title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A system built to support policing work was queried by an officer for a personal purpose, and the queries were run against a person with no connection to any case. The failure sits at the point of use, not in the camera or the database itself: the tool performed as designed for someone holding legitimate credentials.

What would have caught it is a check on why a query was made, not only on who made it. The searches are reported to have occurred repeatedly across two years, which suggests nothing in the workflow flagged repeated lookups of one individual by one officer. Whether any audit, supervisor review or alerting existed at the department is not established by the reporting.

The officer is accused, and a criminal complaint is not a finding of guilt. The reports do not establish his intent, the outcome of the complaint, or what the Select Board will decide.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered Rogers had searched for her location multiple times in 2024 and 2025 using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, and she said he also drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and placed him on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
